scope: Theorem 5.1 (Filled construction) of the manuscript “The spacetime Penrose inequality and enclosing area” (preprints/The-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-and-enclosing-area-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9bb0c350914915db), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix smooth prepared data satisfying Equation (2.1) on a complete one-ended exterior with nonempty compact smooth boundary. In particular, K is compactly supported, g − δ = Od(r2−n) for every fixed d, Rg = O(r−n−β) for some 0 < β < 1, the dominant-energy margin is bounded below by a positive multiple of ϱ−n−β, and every boundary component is strictly future trapped. Fix 0 < ϵ < 1 and n 4 < b1 < min{n − 2, n/2}. Use the filled manifolds MN , weights ρ0, ρ1, ρ, and definitions in Equation (4.3). Choose δ0 > 0 and the polynomial CN as in Lemma 4.3. For all sufficiently large integers N > k = n − 1, there are smooth functions f, Z on MN solving Equation (4.18). The associated function t satisfies −ϵ < t ≤ Z ≤ P(N), ℓ ≤ l(t) ≤ e, |f| + |df|g ≤ exp(P(N)), ℓ = e−Nϵ . (5.1) Here and below P is a polynomial with coefficients depending only on the fixed prepared data, n, ϵ, and the fixed choices in the filling. The height h = ηf, η = ℓ3/2, obeys |h| ≤ C, |h(x)| ≤ Cr(x)−b1 on the original end, (5.2) where C is independent of N. At each fixed N, for every integer j ≥ 0 there are constants CN,j and aN > 0 such that on that end |Dj f| ≤ CN,je−aN r , t, Z = Oj(r2−n ), ∆gt = O(r−n−β ). (5.3) The constants in Equation (5.3), and higher derivative bounds on compact sets, may depend arbitrarily on fixed N.
